survey: A round wall clock seen nearly straight on, tilted slightly so the face reads as a gentle ellipse. It has three main parts. (1) A thick, round orange frame of even width all the way around that holds the face. (2) A flat white face set inside the frame, with 12 navy hour markers evenly spaced at the hour positions and a ring of small navy minute dots just inside the frame, about four between each pair of markers. (3) A hand set on one central pin: a short, wide navy hour hand pointing at about 10, a longer navy minute hand pointing at 2 (the usual 10:10 display pose), and a thin red second hand with a short tail behind the pin, reaching out to the 5 marker. All three hands start at the same red-capped pin and lie flat over the face. The minute hand stops just short of the markers and the hour hand is clearly shorter, so the hands are in the right proportions. The clock hangs against a flat green striped wall and casts a soft shadow, so it reads as wall-mounted. Nothing floats or is loose, and no parts are invented.
